findings.label: M-01 (run-14)
findings.title: setRewardToken (:417-420) undocumented re-arm permanently bricks claim(), the sole permissionless entry point

checks.resolution: Law-3 footgun, IN SCOPE
see XC-2 — code exists and is PoC-exercised

checks.note: root cause is first-party: StableYieldAccumulator.sol:417-420. The streamer only MANIFESTS the revert.

evidence: NatSpec :69-71 states 'Once a nudge share is actually payable there are THREE failure modes' — a closed, affirmatively-exhaustive enumeration, not an illustrative list.

Item 3 of that list names setNudgeAddress as THE re-arm trigger: 'Repointing the sink via setNudgeAddress re-arms exactly that failure mode: register the new (sink, rewardToken) pair on the streamer FIRST.' setRewardToken re-keys the SAME (nudge, rewardToken) stream lookup with identical effect and is absent from the list.
The Required-ops-ordering runbook (:81-90) is a 4-step procedure that likewise never mentions setRewardToken.

setRewardToken (:417-420) emits NO event, while both neighbouring load-bearing setters do — setPhlimbo emits PhlimboUpdated (:415) and setNudgeAddress emits NudgeUpdated (:447). The one setter with a silent catastrophic consequence is the one with no observability.
reckessAdminAdjudication.ruling: NOT reckless-admin-invalid. The invalidating limbs both fail: no malice is required (repointing the reward token is a legitimate, expected operation), and the harm is the OPPOSITE of obvious — the contract's own documentation affirmatively assures the owner that the trigger list is complete and that setRewardToken is not on it. Surprise is not merely plausible here, it is DOCUMENTED IN. A competent, non-malicious operator who reads the runbook, follows all four steps, and calls setRewardToken has done everything right and still bricks the only permissionless entry point, with no event to notice it by. This is the canonical Law-3 footgun.
reckessAdminAdjudication.challengeConsidered: The strongest counter-argument — 'any owner repointing a core token address should re-verify every downstream integration' — was weighed and rejected. It proves too much: it would invalidate every footgun ever, since a hypothetical infinitely-diligent owner re-derives all invariants from scratch. The C4/Law-3 test is not 'could a perfect operator have caught it' but 'would a COMPETENT one be surprised'. A competent operator is entitled to rely on the contract's own exhaustive-by-construction failure-mode list. Rejecting that reliance would also convert F-02 (the doc is falsely complete) into a finding with no consequence, which is incoherent.

findings.unprovenAssumptions: None material. The brick's permanence is affirmatively established rather than assumed: severity-audit-revised cross-checked that no _settle path re-writes s.duration, so only an explicit owner registerStream on the new pair cures it. PoC pins the exact revert selector 0xd62cbfe8 as required for H/M.
findings.notes: The single Medium of the run. Availability limb of C4 Medium; no value component, so the streamer push-semantics correction that withdrew the L-01 raise is structurally incapable of touching it (revert occurs at the registration check before any settle).

findings.rescope: SURVIVES AS A FIRST-PARTY DOCUMENTARY FINDING ONLY. Scope it strictly to the SYA NatSpec leg: :60-64 restates the upstream burst-capture claim one layer up ('the batch-minter receives a smooth linear stream instead of a lumpy push'), which reads to an SYA integrator as a structural guarantee against burst capture. It is not one — the streamer caps the RATE at which value arrives at the sink, never the SIZE any single batchMint caller sweeps from it.
